title: Get something off your chest about rpg maker

posts.author: NaMosca
posts.body:
You know, when I was younger I spent hours messing around with RPG Maker XP, creating my game, my desire was very great, and it still is to tell the truth, but as time went by and I learned about time management and how much work it is to create a game alone and even for RPG Maker XP with simple graphics that probably no one will play, I was getting discouraged, today I even mess around with RPG Maker XP but as soon as I start I feel a sense of disappointment of wasting a huge amount of time, a feeling that I'm wasting time and that makes me stop, although I have this desire to create a game even if it's just for myself, I feel like I'm going to waste a lot of time doing it.
edit: guys that answered me, thank you, its been days I am working 2h each day in my project and really enjoy it, I now have a team (one person until now) and a discord server and we are develop my game
I don't know what happens but since I wrote this post I feel encouraged to persue my dream even if its that only I will play it. I am very happy
we already finish the main story, we are just implementing it

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body: Many of the best-looking jrpg games (not just good-looking, but ones that look like they've had a lot of effort put into them) I've seen here since I started using RPG Maker in 2021 are in STEAM with 20-70 reviews. That's like 500 - 2000 players. So even if you make a game with good looking custom resources and thought-out systems, not many will play it. Just do it if you enjoy the hobby and have some energy to spare.

posts.author: iLLuvitar
posts.body:
It's a labor of love to be honest. I found RPG maker2k waaaaaay back when. My friends from and I still create games with it and send them back and forth to each other for critique some 13ish years later. We fell in love the sandbox get to create your own dream kind of thing.
It really helped me to start making my own resources and getting a bit of personality into my games, and keeping track of your development with notes really solidifies the value of your work imo.

posts.author: TotalyNate
posts.body: Maybe not something to get off my chest but something I just find annoying. It feels like even if you put a lot of effort into your rpg, maybe even if you make your own music and tilesets. People will see your game as "just another rpg maker game" and then write it off as garbage.

posts.author: Beelxiii
posts.body:
I think the worst thing about feeling like you're wasting time with a project is that it's something you care about. If you have a playable game or like 5 prototypes, or hell make a functional door from scratch, then it wasn't a waste of time. You have something to show for it. Not a lot of people can say, "I make games for fun" or "I make a lot of games"
Also, your game isn't "just another rpg maker game" they're your ideas, hopes, and dreams made manifest. Its something you can play and edit or show of to people outside the web who dont even know what rpg maker is.
As long as you like doing what you're doing, it's never a waste of time and you'll have no regrets once you made that thing that you love.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
I could make a laundry list of criticisms about RPG Maker (in fact I have in other threads) but I could likewise make such lists about gamers, the general public, etc.
But I do not expect other parties to change based on my criticisms. It does happen sometimes, but it's just a nice bonus. I simply adapt my own behaviors and expectations.
In response to the OP, I do get overwhelmed by scope creep and lack of progress, but that is my own doing. You will likely just have to scope down your project or break it into more digestable chunks or milestones and realize that it happens to most games. Your favorite game probably has cut content.
If you feel you are wasting your time and no one will play it, make a lot of smaller games that are less time investment. If one takes off, you can dedicate more time to it.

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
One thing I do to reduce scale-creep is to have a "IdeasForNextProject" Libre Office document. I still get a bit of scale-creep (sometime new features do add a lot to the gameplay or are relatively trivial to introduce) but I find it reduces trying out half-baked ideas that will cause re-writes of the current project.
Edit
: That said, I write games primarily for me. Great if anyone else ever looks at them, even better if they were to get some enjoyment from them

To be fair... most of them don't do a lot better than "mediocre" except for maybe graphics, sometimes.  The writing is usually pretty subpar, the systems in place not very well thought-out, the combat not very fun...
The trend is usually "make a stock standard RPG" when it comes to RPG Maker.  Which, isn't bad sometimes.  But, I often bypass RPG Maker games because "they aren't doing anything unique".
My favorite is still Final Fantasy Endless Nova, but not many RPG Maker games ever do as much as that one did or tried to do.
It's less about "how much effort you put in" and more about "putting forth effort in the correct places".

posts.author: AphoticAmaranth
posts.body:
The time that you enjoyed wasting was not wasted. At the very least, you gain experience, if nothing else.
As for things I hate about RPG Maker... a lot, really. I sure do hate having to write $gameVariables.value(69) instead of, y'know, giving variables names that make sense, like most do in literally any other programming language. (Yes I know you can set a name in-editor but that doesn't change the fact that when working with script calls / custom plugins I'd still have to double check, what ID was that variable or state I had to reference again?)
And don't get me started on how they actually manage to make it worse with updates instead of fixing known issues...

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
AphoticAmaranth said:
The time that you enjoyed wasting was not wasted. At the very least, you gain experience, if nothing else.
Click to expand...
This.
I usually like to say to remember to enjoy what you do. I also have said that pretty much all knowledge is worth having. Even if it is just the knowledge that you never want to do something again.
As an aside, coming from someone who has less years in front of them than they have behind them, it is very easy to look back and think how much time you wasted doing different things. Whenever that happens to me, I try to push those thoughts aside and remember that the past is the past and can't be changed. You can learn from it, but there usually isn't much to be gained from dwelling in the past instead of focusing on the now.
And, if I find that I'm not enjoying something anymore, I stop doing it for a while and see if my attitude or outlook changes.
Now, on topic of the original question, I'm sure there are irritations that I have with RPG Maker that I can't readily think of right now, but there are two that spring to mind.
#1 The need for plugins for some things that I would have thought would have just been included in the engine by default. I mean if there were a TON of plugins that many people considered to be essential for MV, why wouldn't you incorporate many of those things as default in MZ?
#2 The fact that most official DLC don't seem to give enough information or screen shots to really tell if it is something you want to buy. And the cost of the DLC too. Which is probably why I haven't bought any DLC.
